stories.title: Blockchain-assisted revocable capability credential authentication for cross-domain UAVs
stories.description: Cross-domain UAV operations require secure and privacy-preserving authentication across multiple administrative domains. However, existing schemes still suffer from centralized authorization, exposure of mission attributes, insufficient revocation consistency, and limited auditability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-assisted revocable capability credential authentication protocol for cross-domain UAV edge networks. The main innovation is to shift cross-domain UAV authentication from identity- or location-centric verification to revocation-aware lifecycle verification of mission capabilities. In the proposed framework, a Domain Authority committee jointly issues blinded capability credentials through distributed key generation and threshold BLS signatures. UAVs then prove mission-policy compliance using Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs without revealing sensitive capability attributes. Meanwhile, the blockchain maintains credential active states, revocation versions, and audit-root evidence for cross-domain consistency and accountability. A ticket-based AuthResume mechanism is further designed to reduce repeated authentication overhead while preventing outdated tickets from bypassing revocation. Formal security analysis, BAN logic, and Scyther verification show that the protocol supports credential unforgeability, revocation enforcement, auditability, mutual authentication, freshness, and session synchronization. Solidity smart contracts were deployed on the Sepolia testnet, and experimental results demonstrate acceptable FullAuth overhead and lightweight repeated access through AuthResume.

stories.title: Enhancing ferric-reducing antioxidant activity through terpene mixture optimization
stories.description: The present study investigated the antioxidant potential of three terpenes p-cymene, thymol, and β-ionone—through their ferric reducing power (FRAP). Individually, p-cymene demonstrated the strongest activity with an EC50 of 123.03 ± 2.05 µg/mL, followed by thymol (EC50 = 153.16 ± 2.84 µg/mL), whereas β-ionone exhibited the lowest ferric reducing capacity (EC50 = 931.46 ± 5.37 µg/mL), revealing significant variation in their antioxidant efficacy. To assess combinatorial effects, twelve randomized mixture trials were performed, each representing the mean of three independent repetitions, yielding FRAP EC50 values ranging from 79.76 to 931.46 µg/mL. Statistical analysis identified significant contributions from linear terms (β1, β2, β3), binary interactions (β12, β13), and the ternary interaction term (β123), indicating that both individual and combined effects shaped the overall antioxidant response. Analysis of 2D and 3D mixture plots suggested that an EC50 around 79.70 µg/mL could be obtained by combining all three terpenes. Furthermore, desirability analysis predicted an optimal FRAP EC50 of 58.23 µg/mL, achieved with a mixture comprising 17% β-ionone, 42% p-cymene, and 41% thymol, with a global desirability of 99.9%. These findings demonstrate that strategic blending of structurally related terpenes can substantially enhance ferric reducing capacity, providing a robust framework for the development of potent natural antioxidant formulations.
